findings.reason: The protected Python solution moves a subtree rooted at node p to become the last child of node q in an N-ary tree. It uses an initial traversal to build a parent mapping for all nodes, checks if p is already a direct child of q (no-op), and walks upward from q to check if q is a descendant of p. If q is inside p's subtree, q is detached first and replaces p in p's parent's children list (or becomes the new root if p was root), before p is appended as q's child. The solution runs in O(n) time and O(n) space; no candidate is required.

Handling the descendant case (q below p) by detaching q first and placing q in p's former position prevents cycles and preserves tree connectivity. Direct child check parent[p] is q correctly returns root unchanged.

Tree traversal to build parent mapping takes O(n) time. Upward ancestor walk and child list reordering take O(n) time. Total time complexity is O(n) with O(n) auxiliary space for parent map and traversal stack. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts root, p, and q nodes, modifying the N-ary tree in place and returning the updated root node.

The approach accurately details pre-move parent mapping, direct-child no-op detection, cycle prevention for q below p, root replacement rules, child list order preservation, and O(n) time / O(n) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover downward subtree DFS vs upward walks, repeated parent search overhead, recursive call stack risks on deep trees, non-direct ancestor cases, q below p cycle traps, root moves, child ordering, and non-last direct child positioning.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the identical parent-map upward-walk subtree move algorithm with SHA-256 digests 602008598ba188a0b9b771266eebdcb540bd4f3b5e9665a75a09c851fdbbb16a and 4f9b3c1a7406976feb169d474aeb54cdccf0e59baf43c652738fdb6bc89bf969.
